rules.title: Do not claim unsafe dual writes are atomic
rules.statement: Durable outbox/intent plus reconciliation; never assume dual writes are atomic.

owner.section: Distributed failure, retries, timeouts, and recovery

applicability.when: One logical operation writes authoritative state and also invokes a broker, provider, cache, or separately owned store.

required_evidence.description: Failure injection before and after each commit or publication boundary converges through durable intent and reconciliation.
required_evidence.validation_method: Crash/failure integration test with duplicate delivery and ambiguous outcome checks.

rules.title: Use exact representations for money
rules.statement: Never store monetary/precision-sensitive values in binary floating point without an explicit, validated reason.

applicability.when: A value represents money, a precision-sensitive quantity, a rate, or an accumulated total whose rounding affects invariants.

conditions: The domain error bound, rounding contract, storage behavior, and cross-language serialization have explicit validation evidence.

required_evidence.description: Boundary, rounding, overflow, serialization, and accumulation cases preserve the declared exact numeric contract.
required_evidence.validation_method: Property and integration tests across API, storage, jobs, and migrations.

rules.title: Bound retries, queues, and timeouts
rules.statement: Never use infinite timeouts or unbounded retries/queues.

applicability.when: Work waits on a dependency, retries an operation, buffers demand, or admits concurrent resource use.

required_evidence.description: Attempts, elapsed time, queue depth, concurrency, payload size, and degraded behavior have explicit finite limits.
required_evidence.validation_method: Overload and dependency-failure test proving admission control, backpressure, and bounded recovery.

rules.title: Treat internal and derived inputs as untrusted
rules.statement: Treat every external, model-generated, cached, imported, or administrator-supplied value as untrusted at its use context.

owner.section: Security, authorization, privacy, and abuse resistance

applicability.when: Data or an instruction crosses a process, service, cache, administrative, import, model, or provider boundary.

required_evidence.description: Every boundary identifies the principal, data provenance, validation, authorization, and secure failure behavior.
required_evidence.validation_method: Threat-model review plus negative tests at the owning service and data boundary.

rules.title: Enforce authorization at the owning boundary
rules.statement: Enforce least privilege in the component that owns the resource; edge filtering, WAFs, and gateways are supplementary.

owner.section: Security, authorization, privacy, and abuse resistance

applicability.when: A protected action or resource can be reached through an API, job, event, admin path, bulk operation, cache, or recovery mechanism.

required_evidence.description: Actor, action, resource, tenant, field, and state checks execute at the owning service or authoritative data boundary.
required_evidence.validation_method: Direct negative requests bypassing frontend and gateway controls, including cross-tenant object access.

rules.title: Prove backups through restore
rules.statement: Never call data protected until a restore has been executed and validated.

applicability.when: A backup, snapshot, replica, archive, or recovery claim is used as evidence of recoverability.

required_evidence.description: An isolated restore reconstructs dependent data, keys, objects, indexes, identities, and event positions within measured RPO/RTO.
required_evidence.validation_method: Recorded restore rehearsal with application-level invariant and business validation.

rules.title: Define multi-region write and conflict semantics
rules.statement: Specify write acknowledgment, read consistency, lag bounds, failover fencing, conflict handling, and behavior during partitions. Do not equate replication with backup.

applicability.when: More than one region can accept authoritative writes or take write authority during failover/failback.

required_evidence.description: Partition, split-brain, failover, old-writer return, conflict, and failback scenarios preserve documented data semantics.
required_evidence.validation_method: Topology-level failure tests with fencing and reconciliation evidence.

rules.title: Keep model proposals outside deterministic authority
rules.statement: The deterministic application owns permissions, budgets, validation, side effects, and durable state; the model proposes text or actions.

applicability.when: A model proposes, selects, or invokes an action that can read protected data, spend resources, mutate durable state, or affect people or systems.

required_evidence.description: Tool execution independently validates schema, policy, permission, budget, idempotency, and approval requirements.
required_evidence.validation_method: Adversarial prompt/tool tests proving model output cannot bypass deterministic controls.

rules.title: Do not let scores waive critical blockers
rules.statement: Never allow checklist completion to substitute for executable controls and tests.

applicability.when: A checklist, rubric, AI-generated contextual score, weighted summary, or model review is used to assess readiness, risk, or approval.

required_evidence.description: Each critical blocker retains an independent pass/fail gate tied to executable controls and tests, regardless of aggregate or contextual scores.
required_evidence.validation_method: Mutation review that raises unrelated scores while leaving a critical control absent and verifies approval remains blocked.
